name: Fall Armyworm (FAW)
visual_symptoms: Pinholes and large ragged shot-holes in whorl leaves; massive sawdust-like brownish frass (excreta) accumulated in the central funnel; inverted Y-shaped suture on the head of caterpillar and 4 raised black spots in a square on 8th abdominal segment.
favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (25-30°C) with dry spells followed by rain; monoculture of hybrid maize.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4 ml/L (60 ml/acre) OR Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4 g/L (80 g/acre) OR Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.5 ml/L, directing spray nozzle directly into the plant whorl.
organic_biological_remedy: Whirl application of Sand + Lime mixture (9:1 ratio); Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) kurstaki @ 2 g/L; Apply Beauveria bassiana or Metarhizium anisopliae @ 5 g/L; Install 5-6 FAW sex pheromone traps per acre.
preventive_measures: Deep summer ploughing to expose pupae to predatory birds; timely planting in synchronized window; intercrop maize with cowpea or desmodium (push-pull strategy); seed treatment with Cyantraniliprole 19.8% + Thiamethoxam 19.8% FS @ 4 ml/kg seed.

name: Pink Bollworm (PBW)
plant_part: Squares, Flowers, Developing Bolls, Cotton Lint
visual_symptoms: 'Rosette flowers' (petals twisted into rosette shape and do not open); premature boll shedding; small exit holes on bolls plugged with excreta; stained and discolored cotton lint with damaged seeds.
favorable_conditions: Late planted cotton, extended crop season (ratooning), warm and humid weather.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Spray Profenofos 50% EC @ 2 ml/L (400 ml/acre) OR Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 2.5 ml/L OR Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.5 g/L; for mature bolls spray Indoxacarb 14.5% SC @ 1 ml/L.
organic_biological_remedy: Install 8-10 Pink Bollworm Pheromone traps (Gossyplure) per acre for monitoring and mass trapping; release Trichogramma bactrae egg parasitoid @ 60,000/acre at weekly intervals; spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Azadirachtin 1500 ppm @ 5 ml/L.
preventive_measures: Plant non-Bt refuge border rows; strictly terminate crop by December end to avoid overwintering; destroy ginning waste and crop stalks; do NOT ratoon cotton.

name: Brown Planthopper (BPH)
visual_symptoms: Browning and drying of plants in circular patches that spread rapidly outward, known as 'Hopper Burn'; thousands of small brown nymphs and adults clustered at the base of tillers just above the water line; sooty mold growing on honeydew exudate.
favorable_conditions: High humidity, stagnant standing water, excessive indiscriminate nitrogen application, dense planting without alleyways.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Drain water from field immediately! Spray Triflumezopyrim 10% SC @ 94 ml/acre OR Pymetrozine 50% WG @ 120 g/acre OR Dinotefuran 20% SG @ 80 g/acre, targeting the base of the plant canopy.
organic_biological_remedy: Spray Neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 2-3 ml/L with liquid detergent; conserve natural predators like Mirid bugs (Cyrtorhinus lividipennis) and Lycosa spiders; avoid broad-spectrum pyrethroids which wipe out predators.
preventive_measures: Provide 30 cm alleyways (pathways) after every 2 meters (8-10 rows) for aeration and sunlight; balance fertilizer with proper Potassium; practice Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD).

name: Yellow Stem Borer
visual_symptoms: Dead Hearts: central leaf shoots dry up and pull out easily during vegetative stage; White Heads (White Ears): completely chaffy, empty white upright panicles during reproductive heading stage.
favorable_conditions: High nitrogen application, continuous rice monoculture, warm cloudy humid weather.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Broadcast Cartap Hydrochloride 4% G @ 8-10 kg/acre OR Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR (Ferterra) @ 4 kg/acre with thin layer of standing water; OR spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3 ml/L.
organic_biological_remedy: Install 5-8 yellow stem borer pheromone traps per acre; clip seedling leaf tips before transplanting to destroy egg masses; release Trichogramma japonicum @ 40,000/acre.
preventive_measures: Clip seedling tips before transplanting; avoid excess urea; harvest paddy close to ground level to eliminate overwintering larvae in stubble.

name: Whitefly & Black Thrips Complex
plant_part: Underside of leaves, Tender apical shoots, Flowers
visual_symptoms: Upward or downward leaf curling, crinkling, stunted boat-shaped leaves; flowers drying and shedding prematurely; tiny silver streaks and bronzing on chilli leaves; tiny white flies flying when plant is shaken; acts as vector transmitting destructive Leaf Curl & Yellow Mosaic Viruses.
favorable_conditions: Warm, dry spells followed by intermittent rain; heavy chemical pesticide resistance.
immediate_chemical_treatment: For Thrips: Spray Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 1 ml/L OR Fipronil 5% SC @ 2 ml/L OR Tolfenpyrad 15% EC @ 2 ml/L. For Whitefly: Spray Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2 g/L OR Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1 ml/L.
organic_biological_remedy: Erect 25-30 Yellow and Blue Sticky Traps per acre; spray Neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 3 ml/L; spray Lecanicillium lecanii bio-fungicide @ 5 g/L; spray Dashparni Ark / Agniastra.
preventive_measures: Grow barrier crops (2-3 border rows of Maize/Sorghum/Bajra) around chilli/cotton fields; apply silver/black reflective plastic mulch; seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70% WS @ 5 g/kg seed.

name: Late Blight of Potato & Tomato
visual_symptoms: Water-soaked irregular pale green/brown lesions starting at leaf margins and tips; during moist cool mornings, a delicate white downy/cottony fungal growth appears on the underside of affected leaves; spreads rapidly across entire field within 48-72 hours turning plants into a rotting foul-smelling black mass; tubers develop purplish brown dry rot.
favorable_conditions: Cool cloudy weather (10-20°C) with relative humidity > 90% and continuous dew or drizzle for 2-3 consecutive days.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Curative systemic spray: Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Curzate) @ 3 g/L OR Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1 g/L + Mancozeb @ 2 g/L OR Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil Gold) @ 2.5 g/L OR Mandipropamid 23.4% SC @ 1 ml/L.
organic_biological_remedy: Preventive spray of Bordeaux mixture (1%) or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L; spray Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L; ensure wide ridge spacing and prompt removal of infected vines.
preventive_measures: Plant certified disease-free tubers of tolerant varieties (Kufri Girdhari, Kufri Khyati); prophylactic spray of Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L before foggy weather strikes; dehaulm vines 10 days before harvest.

name: Yellow Rust (Stripe Rust) of Wheat
visual_symptoms: Bright yellow, powder-like pustules (uredinia) arranged in neat, parallel stripes/lines along the leaf veins; when touched with fingers, bright yellow dust rubs off easily; leaves dry up and turn brown, causing shrivelled grains.
favorable_conditions: Cool temperatures (10-18°C) with persistent fog, dew, and intermittent drizzle in Northern plains and foot-hills.
immediate_chemical_treatment: At the very first appearance of yellow stripes, immediately spray Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 1 ml/L (200 ml in 200 L water per acre) OR Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1 ml/L OR Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1 ml/L.
organic_biological_remedy: Foliar spray of sour buttermilk (fermented chaas @ 50 ml/L) or Panchagavya (3%); field surveillance in northern districts (Punjab, Haryana, Tarai).
preventive_measures: Sow resistant high-yielding varieties recommended by IIWBR (DBW 187/Karan Vandana, DBW 303/Karan Vaishnavi, HD 3086, PBW 725); avoid early October sowing in disease-prone hill slopes.

name: Rice Blast Disease
visual_symptoms: Leaf Blast: Eye-shaped or spindle-shaped lesions with ash-grey centers and dark brown margins; Neck Blast: Node/neck below panicle rots, turns blackish brown and snaps, causing complete failure of grain filling (panicle hangs down chaffy).
favorable_conditions: High relative humidity (>90%), cool night temperatures (18-22°C), excess nitrogenous fertilizer, cloudy weather.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP (Beam) @ 0.6 g/L (120 g/acre) OR Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L OR Kasugamycin 3% SL @ 2 ml/L OR Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1 ml/L.
organic_biological_remedy: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L or 1 kg/acre; treat seeds with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed; spray fermented cow urine + neem extract.
preventive_measures: Treat seeds with Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 2 g/kg seed before sowing; split nitrogen into 3-4 doses; avoid excess urea.

name: Fusarium Wilt
plant_part: Vascular system, Roots, Lower Stem, Foliage
visual_symptoms: Drooping of petioles and leaflets starting from top downwards; leaves lose turgidity, turn dull greenish-yellow, and wilt; when the root or lower stem is split open longitudinally, a prominent brown to black discoloration of vascular xylem vessels is clearly visible.
favorable_conditions: Warm soil temperatures (25-30°C), soil compaction, low organic matter, continuous pulse cultivation.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Drench root zone immediately with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/L OR Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP (Saaf) @ 2.5 g/L OR Copper Oxychloride @ 3 g/L.
organic_biological_remedy: Apply Trichoderma viride or Trichoderma harzianum @ 2.5 kg enriched in 200 kg farmyard manure (FYM) per acre during field preparation; seed treatment with Trichoderma @ 10 g/kg seed.
preventive_measures: Deep summer ploughing; 3-year crop rotation with non-host crops (Sorghum, Pearl millet); grow wilt-resistant varieties (e.g., Chickpea: JG 11, JAKI 9218, Digvijay; Pigeonpea: Asha, BSMR 736).

name: Chilli Leaf Curl Virus (ChLCV)
visual_symptoms: Leaves curl upwards into a boat shape with crinkled puckered surface; severe stunting of internodes resulting in a bushy, dwarf witches' broom appearance; veins become thickened and brittle; flowers drop and little to no fruit set.
favorable_conditions: High population of vector Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) during warm, dry spells.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Viruses cannot be cured once inside the plant! Immediately control the vector Whitefly: Spray Pyriproxyfen 10% + Bifenthrin 10% EC @ 2 ml/L OR Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1 ml/L OR Dinotefuran 20% SG @ 0.5 g/L.
organic_biological_remedy: Uproot and burn virus-infected plants to stop contagion; install 25 yellow sticky traps per acre; spray Neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 3 ml/L; spray sour buttermilk (50 ml/L) mixed with Hing (asafoetida 1 g/L).
preventive_measures: Erect 50-mesh insect-proof nylon nets in nursery beds; grow 3 rows of Maize or Sorghum as tall border barrier; spray systemic insecticide 10 days after transplanting.

name: Nitrogen (N) Deficiency
visual_symptoms: General uniform yellowing (chlorosis) starting on the tips of older bottom leaves and progressing along the midrib in a characteristic 'V' shape (especially in maize); stunted spindly stalks; reduced tillering and light green overall canopy.
favorable_conditions: Sandy soils, waterlogged fields leaching nitrates, drought preventing uptake, low organic matter.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of 2% Urea solution (20 grams Urea per liter of water) OR Nano Urea @ 4 ml/L of water; top-dress Urea @ 25-30 kg/acre if field conditions allow irrigation.
organic_biological_remedy: Apply well-decomposed FYM (5 tonnes/acre) or vermicompost (1 tonne/acre); apply Jeevamrut or enriched Gobar slurry; foliar spray of Panchagavya (3%).
preventive_measures: Follow split application of Nitrogen (Basal, Tillering, Panicle initiation) rather than single heavy dose; apply neem-coated urea to prevent volatilization and leaching; grow green manure crops (Dhaincha / Sunnhemp).

name: Zinc Deficiency (Khaira Disease of Rice)
plant_part: Middle and younger leaves, Base of blade
visual_symptoms: In Rice: Reddish-brown / bronze pigmentation and rusty spots appearing on third and fourth leaves 2-3 weeks after transplanting (Khaira disease); roots turn brown, stunted tillers; In Maize: Broad white / bleached bands on both sides of midrib on new emerging leaves ('White Bud').
favorable_conditions: Calcareous alkaline soils (pH > 7.5), waterlogged cold soils, high phosphorus fertilizer application blocking zinc uptake.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of Zinc Sulphate (heptahydrate 21%) @ 5 g/L mixed with 2.5 g/L of slaked lime (unslaked chuna) or 10 g/L Urea to prevent leaf scorch; OR spray Chelated Zinc (Zn-EDTA 12%) @ 1 g/L.
organic_biological_remedy: Apply enriched vermicompost blended with Zinc-solubilizing bacteria (ZSB - Bacillus sp.) @ 2 kg/acre.
preventive_measures: Basal application of Zinc Sulphate (21%) @ 10-12 kg/acre OR Zinc Sulphate monohydrate (33%) @ 6-8 kg/acre during final puddling/land preparation. Never mix Zinc Sulphate directly with DAP in the same bag!

name: Boron (B) Deficiency / Fruit Cracking
plant_part: Growing tips, Flowers, Developing fruits, Curds
visual_symptoms: Fruit cracking and splitting in Tomato and Pomegranate; hollow stems and brown rot in Cauliflower curds; poor pollen germination causing blossom drop; distorted growing tips with corky tissue on fruit surfaces.
favorable_conditions: Sandy soils subject to leaching, dry soil conditions followed by heavy irrigation, alkaline pH > 7.5.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of Solubor (Di-sodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate 20% Boron) @ 1.0 - 1.5 g/L of water at pre-flowering and fruit development stages.
organic_biological_remedy: Soil application of composted poultry manure or organic seaweed extract containing trace boron.
preventive_measures: Basal soil application of Agricultural Borax (10.5% B) @ 4-5 kg/acre during field preparation; maintain uniform soil moisture to avoid sudden turgor pressure bursts in fruits.

name: Soil Salinity & Sodic Alkaline Crust
visual_symptoms: White crusty salt efflorescence on the soil surface; patchy germination and seed rot; leaf tip scorch and marginal necrosis (burning); severe stunting and poor root penetration; water takes days to infiltrate sodic tight soils.
favorable_conditions: Arid climate, excessive canal irrigation without drainage, rising saline water table, use of brackish borewell water with high EC and SAR.
immediate_chemical_treatment: For Sodic / Alkali Soils (pH > 8.5): Apply Agricultural Gypsum (Calcium Sulphate) based on Gypsum Requirement test (typically 2-4 tonnes/acre); flood with good quality water and leach out sodium after 10 days. For Saline Soils: Flush and leach salts with heavy freshwater irrigation into drainage ditches.
organic_biological_remedy: Green manuring with Dhaincha (Sesbania aculeata) incorporating at 45 days; application of Pressmud (sugar mill filter cake) @ 4-5 tonnes/acre; apply farmyard manure @ 10 tonnes/acre to improve organic carbon buffer.
preventive_measures: Cultivate salt-tolerant crop varieties (Rice: CSR 36, Luna Sankhi; Wheat: KRL 210, KRL 19; Mustard: CS 54, CS 56); install subsurface tile drainage in canal commands; switch to drip irrigation to prevent water table rise.

name: Drought & Extreme Heat Wave Stress
visual_symptoms: Temporary or permanent leaf wilting and rolling; premature drying of flag leaves; scorching of flower petals; forced early maturity leading to shrivelled, pinched grains with drastic test weight drop.
favorable_conditions: Prolonged dry spells > 15 days; daytime temperatures spiking > 36-40°C during grain filling or flowering window.
immediate_chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of Potassium Nitrate (13:0:45) @ 10 g/L (1%) OR Salicylic Acid @ 100 ppm (100 mg/L) OR Glycine Betaine osmoprotectant @ 2 g/L; spray Alpha Naphthyl Acetic Acid (Planofix) @ 0.25 ml/4.5 L to prevent flower drop.
organic_biological_remedy: Apply straw or crop residue mulch (3 inches thick) between crop rows to retain soil moisture and reduce soil surface temperature by 4-6°C; spray bio-stimulants / seaweed extracts @ 2 ml/L.
preventive_measures: Adopt Micro-sprinklers for canopy cooling during midday heat spikes; install drip irrigation; sow heat-tolerant climate-resilient varieties (Wheat: DBW 187, DBW 303; Chickpea: JG 14).
